correctness.rationale: The finite seed is checked by solving the expectile first-order equation piecewise. The difference s2_Y-s2_X is reduced to four exact rational expressions with elementary sign certificates: positive-coefficient numerator on the first interval, a negative discriminant on the second, monotonic positivity from the left endpoint on the third, and the constant 9/50 on the fourth. The sf failure is an exact rational stop-loss computation after exact mean/MAD standardization. The smoothing family has positive density on its full interval support; bounded Wasserstein convergence, unique-root stability of the expectile equation, explicit endpoint extensions at alpha=0 and alpha=1/2, and continuity of stop-loss/MAD preserve both strict inequalities.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly states in Remark 6 that whether the s2 order implies the sf order or conversely is open. Its full skewness section contains only implications from stronger orders. Eberl’s later dissertation studies both expectile-skewness families and proves single-distribution sign equivalence and symmetry characterization, but not a pairwise order implication. Candidate-specific database and web searches for symbols, aliases, exact rational values, and the open-question wording did not locate a covering counterexample or theorem. The residual risk is terminology-based later work not indexed by these expressions.

value.rationale: The direct source explicitly poses the relation between the two expectile-based skewness orders as an open structural question. The finding settles one full implication negatively, not merely a parameter case: it supplies an exact all-alpha s2 ordering, an exact sf reversal, and transfers the counterexample into the source’s atomless interval-support setting. This clarifies the order hierarchy and shows that consistency of two skewness families against common stronger orders does not make one of the weak orders dominate the other.
